1	/**
2	 * Maps one Recently Viewed product onto the subset of `ZimmProductCard` props the
3	 * `recentlyViewed` variation (SFCC-83) actually renders.
4	 *
5	 * **Input source revised 2026-09-08 (build plan §2, "Interim data source") — Einstein is "Not
6	 * Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site, so this build ships against a browser-tracked
7	 * view-history stand-in instead.** Input is now a plain Commerce API `Product`
8	 * (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`), exactly as returned by
9	 * `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own `getProducts` call (`expand: [
10	 * 'prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations']`, `allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`) —
11	 * the same underlying Shopper Products shape the original Einstein-sourced design used, minus the
12	 * Einstein-specific `rec`/flat-`image` wrapper fields `fetchRecProductDetails`
13	 * (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:465-505`) used to bolt on. This
14	 * mapper's own output contract and scope (image-only, no gallery, no was/now pricing — A2's
15	 * `recentlyViewed` variation decision, unchanged) are unaffected; only the shape of what it reads
16	 * on the way in changed, and with it, `selectPrimaryImage`'s fallback below: there is no longer a
17	 * separate flat Einstein image to fall back to, so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no
18	 * usable `src`" and "there is no usable image at all" are now the same case.
19	 *
20	 * Modelled on `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` — no React/react-intl import,
21	 * `formatPrice` injected as a parameter so this module stays independently testable — and on the
22	 * general shape of `liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (`feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`, not this
23	 * branch — read for its approach, not imported). Unlike that demo mapper, this is a production
24	 * path: real `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` SDK types are used directly (AGENTS.md > Type
25	 * Definitions) — with the Einstein-specific input shape gone, there is no longer any hand-rolled
26	 * field on the input type at all.
27	 *
28	 * Deliberately narrow scope, stated here rather than left as a silent gap: this mapper only ever
29	 * returns `currentPrice` (an active selling price), not was/now sale-price detection
30	 * (`originalPrice`) — but that is a scope choice, not a data limitation. **Correction
31	 * (2026-09-08, pre-dates and is unaffected by the input-source revision above):** an earlier
32	 * version of this comment claimed the merged Einstein shape "has no equivalent of"
33	 * `getPriceData`-style pricebook logic — verified inaccurate, and equally true of the plain
34	 * `getProducts` shape this mapper now reads: `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` already requests
35	 * `perPricebook: true`, so `product.tieredPrices` is present, and base SFCC's `getPriceData`
36	 * (`app/utils/product-utils.js`) already derives `listPrice`/`isOnSale` from exactly that field —
37	 * nothing is missing, it's simply not called here. The real reason `originalPrice` isn't mapped is
38	 * that the `recentlyViewed` variation renders no price at all today (see
39	 * `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s `recentlyViewed` `VARIATION_CONFIG` row — `showContent: false`), so
40	 * there is nothing for it to feed. Mapping `currentPrice` anyway costs nothing and means a future
41	 * consumer of this same mapper (e.g. a variation that does render price) isn't blocked on this
42	 * file being revisited — extending it to also call `getPriceData` at that point would be a small,
43	 * well-precedented addition, not new pricebook work.
44	 */
45	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
46	import { filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
47	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
48	import type { ZimmProductCardBaseProps, ZimmProductCardImage } from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
49	
50	/**
51	 * The real Commerce API `Product` (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
52	 * — not hand-rolled). A plain alias, not an augmentation: unlike the pre-revision Einstein-sourced
53	 * shape this replaces, `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s plain `getProducts` result needs nothing
54	 * bolted on — `Product.id` is used directly, and there is no separate flat-image field. Kept as a
55	 * named alias (rather than importing `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` directly at each call site)
56	 * so this module's own input type has a name that documents its role here.
57	 */
58	export type RecentlyViewedProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product;
59	
60	/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl,
61	 *  mirroring `productInfo.ts`'s own `FormatPrice` shape. */
62	export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
63	
64	/**
65	 * The subset of `ZimmProductCardBaseProps` this mapper populates. Deliberately excludes
66	 * `headingLevel` and `variation` — both are render-context decisions belonging to the container
67	 * step that maps recs through this mapper and renders the rail (SFCC-83's A6 step), which supplies
68	 * `headingLevel` uniformly for every card and adds `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` itself when
69	 * spreading this output into `<ZimmProductCard>` — the rail organism itself (A5) takes already-full
70	 * `ZimmProductCardProps` objects, so variation must already be set before it sees them. A pure data
71	 * mapper choosing a heading level would conflate a data concern with a layout one. Also excludes `hoverImage`/`images` — this
72	 * mapper only ever returns one image (`primaryImage`); see `selectPrimaryImage`'s own docblock
73	 * for why.
74	 */
75	export type RecentlyViewedCard = Pick<
76	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
77	  'id' | 'href' | 'name' | 'primaryImage' | 'primaryImageFallbacks' | 'currentPrice'
78	>;
79	
80	/** The correctly-sized product image view, per AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance: never serve an
81	 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size. Named rather than inlined per conventions.md's
82	 *  no-magic-strings rule — this is a real, semantic SFCC image `viewType` key. */
83	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
84	
85	/**
86	 * Resolves the one image this mapper ever returns. `hoverImage`/`images` are never populated —
87	 * SFCC-83 AC 3 asks for "the product's index image" (singular), and the `recentlyViewed`
88	 * variation renders neither a hover-swap nor a gallery (see `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
89	 * `recentlyViewed` row: `showHoverImageSwap: false`, and its render branch never forwards
90	 * `images` at all).
91	 *
92	 * Uses `filterImageGroups` at `viewType: 'medium'` (a real, correctly-sized product image) —
93	 * `variationValues` is deliberately empty: a Recently Viewed product is already one specific
94	 * product, not a search hit needing a variant pick the way `liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts`'s own
95	 * `resolveDemoVariant` handles, so that logic does not apply here.
96	 *
97	 * **No flat-image fallback (2026-09-08 input-source revision).** The pre-revision Einstein-merged
98	 * shape carried its own flat `image.disBaseLink`/`image.alt` (Einstein's own single-reference
99	 * thumbnail) to fall back to when `imageGroups` filtering came up empty. The plain
100	 * `getProducts` shape this mapper now reads has no equivalent field at all — `imageGroups` is the
101	 * only image source there is — so "the selected `imageGroups` image has no usable `src`" and
102	 * "there is no usable image at all" have collapsed into the same case; both now return `null`.
103	 *
104	 * **Also returns `fallbacks` — the rest of the same matched image group (2026-09-08, live
105	 * defect).** Confirmed live against product `4673TS251`: its `medium` group has 9 real images,
106	 * but index 0 specifically 404s (a stale/unpublished catalog image reference) while the other 8
107	 * resolve fine — `filterImageGroups`/`[0]` alone had no way to route around a single bad entry
108	 * sitting ahead of good ones in the same group. `fallbacks` is every OTHER image in that same
109	 * matched group, in order, for `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own cascading `primaryImageFallbacks`
110	 * prop to try if the chosen primary image fails to load — see that component's own JSDoc for the
111	 * full mechanism. Not a new image *source*, just no longer silently discarding the 8 working
112	 * images that were already sitting right next to the one broken one.
113	 *
114	 * @returns `null` when there is no usable `src`. `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and
115	 *   non-empty, so there is no safe placeholder card to build without a real image — "no usable
116	 *   image" is treated the same as "no usable name" in `selectRecentlyViewedCard` below: a hard
117	 *   gate that yields no card at all. Returning `null` here is the only option that structurally
118	 *   cannot violate the non-empty-`alt` contract, since there is no returned object for `alt` to
119	 *   be empty on.
120	 */
121	const selectPrimaryImage = (
122	  product: RecentlyViewedProduct,
123	  productName: string,
124	): { image: ZimmProductCardImage; fallbacks: ZimmProductCardImage[] } | null => {
125	  const filteredGroups = filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
126	    viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
127	    variationValues: {},
128	  }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[];
129	  const groupImages = filteredGroups[0]?.images ?? [];
130	  const [groupImage, ...remainingGroupImages] = groupImages;
131	  if (!groupImage) return null;
132	
133	  const src = groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link;
134	  if (!src) return null;
135	
136	  // ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt is required and non-empty (unlike base ProductTile's
137	  // decorative alt: '' convention) — mirrors liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts's own fallback exactly.
138	  const alt = groupImage.alt?.trim() || productName;
139	  const fallbacks = remainingGroupImages
140	    .map((fallbackImage) => {
141	      const fallbackSrc = fallbackImage.disBaseLink || fallbackImage.link;
142	      if (!fallbackSrc) return null;
143	      return { src: fallbackSrc, alt: fallbackImage.alt?.trim() || productName };
144	    })
145	    .filter((fallbackImage): fallbackImage is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(fallbackImage));
146	
147	  return { image: { src, alt }, fallbacks };
148	};
149	
150	/**
151	 * @param product - A plain Commerce API product from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
152	 *   `getProducts` call, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
153	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
154	 * @returns Props for the `recentlyViewed` `ZimmProductCard` variation, or `null` when the product
155	 *   has no usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw.
156	 */
157	export const selectRecentlyViewedCard = (
158	  product: RecentlyViewedProduct | undefined | null,
159	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
160	): RecentlyViewedCard | null => {
161	  if (!product?.name) return null;
162	
163	  const selectedImage = selectPrimaryImage(product, product.name);
164	  if (!selectedImage) return null;
165	
166	  return {
167	    id: product.id,
168	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id }),
169	    name: product.name,
170	    primaryImage: selectedImage.image,
171	    primaryImageFallbacks: selectedImage.fallbacks,
172	    // No hardcoded fallback currency — if either is absent, skip formatting rather than guess,
173	    // matching productInfo.ts's own "no hardcoded fallback currency" comment.
174	    currentPrice:
175	      typeof product.price === 'number' && product.currency ? formatPrice(product.price, product.currency) : undefined,
176	  };
177	};

1	import type { ShopperSearchTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
2	import { getPriceData, filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
3	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
4	import type {
5	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
6	  ZimmProductCardPlpVariation,
7	  ZimmProductCardImage,
8	} from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
9	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';
10	
11	// This mapper is PLP-only by design, so it returns the narrowed shape directly rather than the
12	// full `ZimmProductCardProps` union — letting a caller pass the result straight to a
13	// PLP-typed component (like this page's own `ProductListCard`) with no re-narrowing needed.
14	type ProductListCardResult = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardPlpVariation;
15	
16	/**
17	 * `c_productBadges` is a custom SFCC attribute (SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI hook) with no
18	 * typed field on the base SDK's `ProductSearchHit` — it only reaches this shape via that type's
19	 * own `{[key: string]: any}` index signature. Narrowed here to the one shape this mapper reads,
20	 * rather than trusting `any` at every call site.
21	 */
22	export type ProductListSearchHit = ShopperSearchTypes.ProductSearchHit & {
23	  c_productBadges?: Array<{ productBadge?: string }>;
24	};
25	
26	type RawImage = { alt?: string; disBaseLink?: string; link?: string };
27	
28	const toCardImage = (image: RawImage | undefined): ZimmProductCardImage | undefined => {
29	  const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
30	  if (!src) return undefined;
31	  return { src, alt: image?.alt ?? '' };
32	};
33	
34	/** The correctly-sized product image view the colour+viewType-scoped trio below all read — never
35	 *  serve an arbitrary-sized image at gallery/thumbnail size (AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance).
36	 *  Matches `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s / `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own identically-named,
37	 *  identically-valued constant. Named per conventions.md's no-magic-strings rule. */
38	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
39	
40	/**
41	 * The real, live SFCC `variationAttributes`/`variationValues` id for colour — confirmed directly
42	 * against a real 2-colour product (`ZWNEWPRD04`, colours BLK/TAN), each with its own separate
43	 * `imageGroups` entry tagged `variationAttributes: [{id: 'color', values: [{value: 'BLK'}]}]`.
44	 * Named per conventions.md's no-magic-strings rule. American spelling because this documents the
45	 * real, live SFCC attribute id (data, not a Zimmermann-authored identifier) — see
46	 * `resolveRepresentativeColour` below for the Australian-spelled function/variable naming this
47	 * constant feeds.
48	 */
49	const COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';
50	
51	/**
52	 * Resolves the colour SFCC's own search index already chose to represent this hit — added
53	 * 2026-09-09 (plan addendum §7, step C1) to close a confirmed live defect: this mapper's gallery
54	 * used to be picked with no colour (or viewType) filter at all — "whichever image group has the
55	 * most images" — so a multi-colour product's gallery could show the wrong colour's photos.
56	 * Confirmed live against a real 2-colour product (`ZWNEWPRD04`, BLK/TAN): each colour has its own
57	 * separate, explicitly-tagged `imageGroups` entry, so the old "most images wins" heuristic could
58	 * (and did) pick the wrong one whenever the off-colour group happened to have more photos.
59	 *
60	 * `hit.representedProduct.id` is the specific variant SFCC's search index already picked to
61	 * represent this (typically master-level) hit; matching it against `hit.variants[]` by
62	 * `productId` finds that exact variant's own `variationValues.color` — deterministic and
63	 * server-decided, no guessing and no reliance on the untyped `c_color` custom attribute. There is
64	 * no colour selector on this card and none is being added here — this only teaches the mapper to
65	 * respect the colour SFCC already chose, not to let the shopper pick a different one.
66	 *
67	 * @returns `undefined` when there is no `representedProduct`, no `variants` array, or no variant
68	 *   whose `productId` matches it — callers scope to `viewType` alone in that case (see
69	 *   `selectColourScopedImages` below), never back to the old fully-unscoped "biggest group
70	 *   anywhere" pick.
71	 */
72	export const resolveRepresentativeColour = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): string | undefined => {
73	  const representedProductId = hit.representedProduct?.id;
74	  if (!representedProductId) return undefined;
75	
76	  const representativeVariant = hit.variants?.find(
77	    (variant) => variant.productId === representedProductId,
78	  );
79	  return representativeVariant?.variationValues?.[COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID];
80	};
81	
82	/**
83	 * The colour+viewType-scoped image array `selectGalleryImages`, `hoverImage`, and
84	 * `primaryImageFallbacks` are all derived from — resolved via `resolveRepresentativeColour` so
85	 * all three read the same deterministic colour. Replaces the old viewType/colour-agnostic
86	 * "whichever group has the most images" pick entirely (plan addendum §7, step C1, 2026-09-09) —
87	 * when no colour resolves (single-colour product, or no `variants`/`representedProduct` match),
88	 * this still scopes to `viewType: 'medium'` alone and never falls back to that old fully-unscoped
89	 * behaviour.
90	 *
91	 * Only the first matching image group is read (`filteredGroups[0]`), matching
92	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s / `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own `selectPrimaryImage`
93	 * precedent for the same `filterImageGroups` call — a colour+viewType pair identifies at most one
94	 * real group in practice, so there is nothing to gain from reading past the first match.
95	 *
96	 * `hit.image` (the required `primaryImage` slot) is untouched by this and resolved exactly as
97	 * before by `selectProductListCard` — this array only ever supplies the gallery/hover-swap/
98	 * fallback candidates, never the primary image itself.
99	 */
100	const selectColourScopedImages = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): ZimmProductCardImage[] => {
101	  const colour = resolveRepresentativeColour(hit);
102	  const filteredGroups = filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups ?? [], {
103	    viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
104	    variationValues: colour ? { [COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour } : {},
105	  }) as ShopperSearchTypes.ImageGroup[];
106	
107	  const groupImages = filteredGroups[0]?.images ?? [];
108	  return groupImages.map(toCardImage).filter((img): img is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(img));
109	};
110	
111	/**
112	 * Picks this hit's gallery from the colour+viewType-scoped image array (see
113	 * `selectColourScopedImages` above) — rebuilt 2026-09-09 (plan addendum §7, step C1) to replace
114	 * the old viewType/colour-agnostic "biggest group anywhere" pick, a confirmed live defect (see
115	 * `selectColourScopedImages`'s own docblock). Returns `undefined` for 0 or 1 resulting images,
116	 * matching `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own "no gallery" contract for that case — this function
117	 * doesn't duplicate that check, it just never returns a 1-length array.
118	 */
119	export const selectGalleryImages = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): ZimmProductCardImage[] | undefined => {
120	  const images = selectColourScopedImages(hit);
121	  return images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;
122	};
123	
124	/**
125	 * Reads the "size" variation attribute (if this hit has one) into the shape
126	 * `ZimmSizeChipGroup` expects. `orderable` on each value already reflects real stock per that
127	 * specific size, so it maps directly to `isDisabled` with no extra lookup needed.
128	 */
129	export const selectSizeChipValues = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): ZimmSizeChipValue[] => {
130	  const sizeAttribute = hit.variationAttributes?.find((attr) => attr.id === 'size');
131	  return (sizeAttribute?.values ?? []).map((value) => ({
132	    value: value.value,
133	    label: value.name ?? value.value,
134	    isDisabled: value.orderable === false,
135	  }));
136	};
137	
138	/** What `resolveOrderableVariant` resolves a selected size chip value to — the real, orderable
139	 *  SKU for that specific size, not the master/represented-product id this hit otherwise defaults
140	 *  to. `price` is the variant's own (`ShopperSearchTypes.Variant`'s own field, confirmed real via
141	 *  a live product-detail check, 2026-09-08), which can genuinely differ from the hit's own flat
142	 *  `price` across sizes (e.g. plus sizes priced higher) — callers should prefer this over the
143	 *  hit's own price once a variant has been resolved. */
144	export type ResolvedVariant = {
145	  productId: string;
146	  price: number | undefined;
147	  orderable: boolean;
148	};
149	
150	/**
151	 * Resolves a selected size CHIP VALUE to its real orderable variant — added 2026-09-08 (Gap 3:
152	 * "size-aware Add to Bag" was previously cosmetic; selecting a chip never changed what got added
153	 * to the bag at all). Confirmed live against product `4673TS251`: `hit.variants` is real and
154	 * populated (`expand: [...,'variations']`, already requested by this page's own search call),
155	 * each entry carrying its own real `productId` (e.g. `4673TS251GVSCP0P`) keyed by
156	 * `variationValues.size` (e.g. `'0P'`) — exactly the lookup this function performs.
157	 *
158	 * Returns `null` when there is no matching variant at all (no `variants` array, or no entry
159	 * whose `variationValues.size` equals `sizeValue`) — callers are expected to fall back to this
160	 * hit's own default `representedProduct`/`productId` resolution in that case, the same default

192	};

194	/**

198	 * and `getPriceData` for the other). No `opts` passed — the default `quantity: 1` is correct for

202	 * **Closes 2026-09-08's confirmed gap**: this hit's own `perPricebook: true` + `expand: [...,
203	 * 'prices']` request (product-list/index.tsx) does carry real tiered pricing — checked directly
204	 * against a live on-sale product via the Shopper Products detail endpoint (same underlying
205	 * pricebook data; the search endpoint's own live response couldn't be intercepted directly, since
206	 * this page's initial data arrives via SSR with no separate client-side request to inspect) —
207	 * closing the honest "not checked against a live hit" caveat this file's own history carried.
208	 */

210	  hit: ProductListSearchHit,
211	  formatPrice: (amount: number, currency: string) => string,
212	): Pick<ProductListCardResult, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
213	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(hit);
214	
215	  const currentPrice =

217	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, hit.currency)
218	      : undefined;

221	  // identical to its current one.

1	import type { ShopperSearchTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
2	import { getPriceData, filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
3	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
4	import type {
5	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
6	  ZimmProductCardPlpVariation,
7	  ZimmProductCardImage,
8	} from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
9	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';
10	
11	// This mapper is PLP-only by design, so it returns the narrowed shape directly rather than the
12	// full `ZimmProductCardProps` union — letting a caller pass the result straight to a
13	// PLP-typed component (like this page's own `ProductListCard`) with no re-narrowing needed.
14	type ProductListCardResult = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardPlpVariation;
15	
16	/**
17	 * `c_productBadges` is a custom SFCC attribute (SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI hook) with no
18	 * typed field on the base SDK's `ProductSearchHit` — it only reaches this shape via that type's
19	 * own `{[key: string]: any}` index signature. Narrowed here to the one shape this mapper reads,
20	 * rather than trusting `any` at every call site.
21	 */
22	export type ProductListSearchHit = ShopperSearchTypes.ProductSearchHit & {
23	  c_productBadges?: Array<{ productBadge?: string }>;
24	};
25	
26	type RawImage = { alt?: string; disBaseLink?: string; link?: string };
27	
28	const toCardImage = (image: RawImage | undefined): ZimmProductCardImage | undefined => {
29	  const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
30	  if (!src) return undefined;
31	  return { src, alt: image?.alt ?? '' };
32	};
33	
34	/** The correctly-sized product image view the colour+viewType-scoped trio below all read — never
35	 *  serve an arbitrary-sized image at gallery/thumbnail size (AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance).
36	 *  Matches `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s / `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own identically-named,
37	 *  identically-valued constant. Named per conventions.md's no-magic-strings rule. */
38	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
39	
40	/**
41	 * The real, live SFCC `variationAttributes`/`variationValues` id for colour — confirmed directly
42	 * against a real 2-colour product (`ZWNEWPRD04`, colours BLK/TAN), each with its own separate
43	 * `imageGroups` entry tagged `variationAttributes: [{id: 'color', values: [{value: 'BLK'}]}]`.
44	 * Named per conventions.md's no-magic-strings rule. American spelling because this documents the
45	 * real, live SFCC attribute id (data, not a Zimmermann-authored identifier) — see
46	 * `resolveRepresentativeColour` below for the Australian-spelled function/variable naming this
47	 * constant feeds.
48	 */
49	const COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';
50	
51	/**
52	 * Resolves the colour SFCC's own search index already chose to represent this hit — added
53	 * 2026-09-09 (plan addendum §7, step C1) to close a confirmed live defect: this mapper's gallery
54	 * used to be picked with no colour (or viewType) filter at all — "whichever image group has the
55	 * most images" — so a multi-colour product's gallery could show the wrong colour's photos.
56	 * Confirmed live against a real 2-colour product (`ZWNEWPRD04`, BLK/TAN): each colour has its own
57	 * separate, explicitly-tagged `imageGroups` entry, so the old "most images wins" heuristic could
58	 * (and did) pick the wrong one whenever the off-colour group happened to have more photos.
59	 *
60	 * `hit.representedProduct.id` is the specific variant SFCC's search index already picked to
61	 * represent this (typically master-level) hit; matching it against `hit.variants[]` by
62	 * `productId` finds that exact variant's own `variationValues.color` — deterministic and
63	 * server-decided, no guessing and no reliance on the untyped `c_color` custom attribute. There is
64	 * no colour selector on this card and none is being added here — this only teaches the mapper to
65	 * respect the colour SFCC already chose, not to let the shopper pick a different one.
66	 *
67	 * @returns `undefined` when there is no `representedProduct`, no `variants` array, or no variant
68	 *   whose `productId` matches it — callers scope to `viewType` alone in that case (see
69	 *   `selectColourScopedImages` below), never back to the old fully-unscoped "biggest group
70	 *   anywhere" pick.
71	 */
72	export const resolveRepresentativeColour = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): string | undefined => {
73	  const representedProductId = hit.representedProduct?.id;
74	  if (!representedProductId) return undefined;
75	
76	  const representativeVariant = hit.variants?.find((variant) => variant.productId === representedProductId);
77	  return representativeVariant?.variationValues?.[COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID];
78	};
79	
80	/**
81	 * The colour+viewType-scoped image array `selectGalleryImages`, `hoverImage`, and
82	 * `primaryImageFallbacks` are all derived from — resolved via `resolveRepresentativeColour` so
83	 * all three read the same deterministic colour. Replaces the old viewType/colour-agnostic
84	 * "whichever group has the most images" pick entirely (plan addendum §7, step C1, 2026-09-09) —
85	 * when no colour resolves (single-colour product, or no `variants`/`representedProduct` match),
86	 * this still scopes to `viewType: 'medium'` alone and never falls back to that old fully-unscoped
87	 * behaviour.
88	 *
89	 * Only the first matching image group is read (`filteredGroups[0]`), matching
90	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s / `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own `selectPrimaryImage`
91	 * precedent for the same `filterImageGroups` call — a colour+viewType pair identifies at most one
92	 * real group in practice, so there is nothing to gain from reading past the first match.
93	 *
94	 * `hit.image` (the required `primaryImage` slot) is untouched by this and resolved exactly as
95	 * before by `selectProductListCard` — this array only ever supplies the gallery/hover-swap/
96	 * fallback candidates, never the primary image itself.
97	 */
98	const selectColourScopedImages = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): ZimmProductCardImage[] => {
99	  const colour = resolveRepresentativeColour(hit);
100	  const filteredGroups = filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups ?? [], {
101	    viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
102	    variationValues: colour ? { [COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour } : {},
103	  }) as ShopperSearchTypes.ImageGroup[];
104	
105	  const groupImages = filteredGroups[0]?.images ?? [];
106	  return groupImages.map(toCardImage).filter((img): img is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(img));
107	};
108	
109	/**
110	 * Picks this hit's gallery from the colour+viewType-scoped image array (see
111	 * `selectColourScopedImages` above) — rebuilt 2026-09-09 (plan addendum §7, step C1) to replace
112	 * the old viewType/colour-agnostic "biggest group anywhere" pick, a confirmed live defect (see
113	 * `selectColourScopedImages`'s own docblock). Returns `undefined` for 0 or 1 resulting images,
114	 * matching `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own "no gallery" contract for that case — this function
115	 * doesn't duplicate that check, it just never returns a 1-length array.
116	 */
117	export const selectGalleryImages = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): ZimmProductCardImage[] | undefined => {
118	  const images = selectColourScopedImages(hit);
119	  return images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;
120	};
121	
122	/**
123	 * Reads the "size" variation attribute (if this hit has one) into the shape
124	 * `ZimmSizeChipGroup` expects. `orderable` on each value already reflects real stock per that
125	 * specific size, so it maps directly to `isDisabled` with no extra lookup needed.
126	 */
127	export const selectSizeChipValues = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): ZimmSizeChipValue[] => {
128	  const sizeAttribute = hit.variationAttributes?.find((attr) => attr.id === 'size');
129	  return (sizeAttribute?.values ?? []).map((value) => ({
130	    value: value.value,
131	    label: value.name ?? value.value,
132	    isDisabled: value.orderable === false,
133	  }));
134	};
135	
136	/** What `resolveOrderableVariant` resolves a selected size chip value to — the real, orderable
137	 *  SKU for that specific size, not the master/represented-product id this hit otherwise defaults
138	 *  to. `price` is the variant's own (`ShopperSearchTypes.Variant`'s own field, confirmed real via
139	 *  a live product-detail check, 2026-09-08), which can genuinely differ from the hit's own flat
140	 *  `price` across sizes (e.g. plus sizes priced higher) — callers should prefer this over the
141	 *  hit's own price once a variant has been resolved. */
142	export type ResolvedVariant = {
143	  productId: string;
144	  price: number | undefined;
145	  orderable: boolean;
146	};
147	
148	/**
149	 * Resolves a selected size CHIP VALUE to its real orderable variant — added 2026-09-08 (Gap 3:
150	 * "size-aware Add to Bag" was previously cosmetic; selecting a chip never changed what got added
151	 * to the bag at all). Confirmed live against product `4673TS251`: `hit.variants` is real and
152	 * populated (`expand: [...,'variations']`, already requested by this page's own search call),
153	 * each entry carrying its own real `productId` (e.g. `4673TS251GVSCP0P`) keyed by
154	 * `variationValues.size` (e.g. `'0P'`) — exactly the lookup this function performs.
155	 *
156	 * Returns `null` when there is no matching variant at all (no `variants` array, or no entry
157	 * whose `variationValues.size` equals `sizeValue`) — callers are expected to fall back to this
158	 * hit's own default `representedProduct`/`productId` resolution in that case, the same default
159	 * that already existed before size-aware add-to-bag was ever selectable.
160	 */
161	export const resolveOrderableVariant = (hit: ProductListSearchHit, sizeValue: string): ResolvedVariant | null => {
162	  const variant = hit.variants?.find((candidate) => candidate.variationValues?.size === sizeValue);
163	  if (!variant) return null;
164	
165	  return {
166	    productId: variant.productId,
167	    price: variant.price,
168	    orderable: variant.orderable !== false,
169	  };
170	};
171	
172	/**
173	 * `getPriceData`'s own return shape (base SFCC, `product-utils.js:123-170`), narrowed to the
174	 * three fields this mapper reads — ported verbatim from `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own
175	 * identically-named type, same reasoning: `@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no types for this
176	 * subpath (falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s catch-all ambient `any`), so this
177	 * documents an assumed shape rather than letting `any` propagate — the real correctness proof is
178	 * this file's own test comparing against a real `getPriceData` call, not this annotation alone.
179	 */
180	type SfccPriceData = {
181	  /** `findLowestPrice()`'s own `minPrice` — replaces the flat `hit.price` field this mapper used
182	   *  to read for `currentPrice` (2026-09-08: now sourced from the same call as `originalPrice`,
183	   *  closing the "two fields could disagree on a multi-variant hit" gap the old code risked). */
184	  currentPrice: number;
185	  /** The highest tiered price found — "was" price. `undefined` when the hit has no
186	   *  `tieredPrices` at all (there is then no maximum to compute). */
187	  listPrice: number | undefined;
188	  /** `currentPrice < listPrice` — always `false`, never `true`, when `listPrice` is `undefined`. */
189	  isOnSale: boolean;
190	};
191	
192	/**
193	 * Derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from a single `getPriceData(hit)` call — ported verbatim
194	 * from `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own `selectPriceFields` (see that file's own docblock
195	 * for why both fields must come from the one call rather than mixing a flat price field for one
196	 * and `getPriceData` for the other). No `opts` passed — the default `quantity: 1` is correct for
197	 * a single-unit card display. No hardcoded fallback currency — if either the price or the
198	 * currency is absent, formatting is skipped rather than guessed.
199	 *
200	 * **Closes 2026-09-08's confirmed gap**: this hit's own `perPricebook: true` + `expand: [...,
201	 * 'prices']` request (product-list/index.tsx) does carry real tiered pricing — checked directly
202	 * against a live on-sale product via the Shopper Products detail endpoint (same underlying
203	 * pricebook data; the search endpoint's own live response couldn't be intercepted directly, since
204	 * this page's initial data arrives via SSR with no separate client-side request to inspect) —
205	 * closing the honest "not checked against a live hit" caveat this file's own history carried.
206	 */
207	const selectPriceFields = (
208	  hit: ProductListSearchHit,
209	  formatPrice: (amount: number, currency: string) => string,
210	): Pick<ProductListCardResult, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
211	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(hit);
212	
213	  const currentPrice =
214	    typeof priceData.currentPrice === 'number' && hit.currency
215	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, hit.currency)
216	      : undefined;
217	
218	  // Only set when isOnSale is true -- a not-on-sale hit must not render a crossed-out price
219	  // identical to its current one.
220	  const originalPrice =
221	    priceData.isOnSale && typeof priceData.listPrice === 'number' && hit.currency
222	      ? formatPrice(priceData.listPrice, hit.currency)
223	      : undefined;
224	
225	  return { currentPrice, originalPrice };
226	};
227	
228	/**
229	 * Maps one real product-search hit to `ZimmProductCardProps` (`variation: 'plp'`) for this quick
230	 * test integration. `formatPrice` is passed in rather than built here — the page already owns an
231	 * `intl`-based formatter, and this stays a pure function with no `react-intl` dependency of its
232	 * own, the same split the page's existing wishlist-toast handlers already follow.
233	 *
234	 * Returns `null` when there's no usable name or primary image — mirrors `ZimmProductName`'s own
235	 * "no render without a name" contract, and `ZimmProductCardBaseProps.primaryImage`'s required-ness
236	 * (a card with neither has nothing to legitimately render).
237	 *
238	 * **`hoverImage`/`primaryImageFallbacks` added 2026-09-09 (plan addendum §7, step C1)** — both
239	 * read off the same colour+viewType-scoped array `images` is built from (see
240	 * `selectColourScopedImages`), never off `hit.image`. `hit.image` (`primaryImage` above) is
241	 * untouched by this addendum and still resolved exactly as before.
242	 */
243	export const selectProductListCard = (
244	  hit: ProductListSearchHit,
245	  formatPrice: (amount: number, currency: string) => string,
246	): ProductListCardResult | null => {
247	  const primaryImage = toCardImage(hit.image);
248	  if (!hit.productName || !primaryImage) return null;
249	
250	  const { currentPrice, originalPrice } = selectPriceFields(hit, formatPrice);
251	
252	  // hoverImage/primaryImageFallbacks are the second entry and the remainder of the same
253	  // colour+viewType-scoped array `images` (below) is built from — see
254	  // `selectColourScopedImages`'s own docblock. Computed via a second, independent call so
255	  // `selectGalleryImages` keeps its own single-argument, independently-testable public signature
256	  // rather than needing the array threaded in. `hit.image` (primaryImage above) is untouched by
257	  // this — it stays the sole source for primaryImage, exactly as before.
258	  const colourScopedImages = selectColourScopedImages(hit);
259	  const hoverImage = colourScopedImages[1];
260	  const primaryImageFallbacks = colourScopedImages.slice(2);
261	
262	  return {
263	    id: hit.productId,
264	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: hit.productId }),
265	    name: hit.productName,
266	    headingLevel: 'h3',
267	    primaryImage,
268	    primaryImageFallbacks,
269	    hoverImage,
270	    images: selectGalleryImages(hit),
271	    currentPrice,
272	    originalPrice,
273	    isUnavailable: hit.orderable === false,
274	    // Single highest-priority badge — SFCC-225's own confirmed shape (see the organism's own
275	    // docblock, "Badge count" note): only one badge is ever shown, never a list.
276	    badge: hit.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge,
277	    variation: 'plp',
278	    sizeChipValues: selectSizeChipValues(hit),
279	  };
280	};
281

## Summary

Branch confirmed: `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed` (not `develop`/`main` — no hook conflict).

Implemented per `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md` §7 Addendum, step **C1 — Colour-aware image resolution in the PLP mapper** (lines 1425–1450), per the task's own restated core requirement. Touched only the two named files.

### Files changed

**`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts`**
- Added `filterImageGroups` to the existing `product-utils` import.
- Added `resolveRepresentativeColour(hit)` (exported, JSDoc'd): finds `hit.variants[]` entry whose `productId` matches `hit.representedProduct?.id`, returns that entry's `variationValues?.color`, `undefined` on any miss.
- Added a private `selectColourScopedImages(hit)` helper: calls `filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups ?? [], {viewType: 'medium', variationValues: colour ? {color: colour} : {}})`, reads `filteredGroups[0]?.images`, maps through the existing (untouched) `toCardImage`.
- Rebuilt `selectGalleryImages` to be a thin wrapper: `images.length > 1 ? images : undefined` over `selectColourScopedImages(hit)` — the old "biggest group across every viewType/colour" `.reduce()` logic is gone entirely.
- In `selectProductListCard`: added `const colourScopedImages = selectColourScopedImages(hit); const hoverImage = colourScopedImages[1]; const primaryImageFallbacks = colourScopedImages.slice(2);`, and added both fields to the returned object. `hit.image` → `primaryImage` resolution is untouched (same `toCardImage(hit.image)` call, same position in the function).
- Named constants `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE`/`COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID` added (no magic strings), with a comment explaining the American-spelling-for-real-SFCC-data-key vs. Australian-spelling-for-Zimmermann-identifiers split.

**`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.test.ts`**
- Added `MULTI_COLOUR_HIT` fixture mirroring the real `ZWNEWPRD04` BLK/TAN shape, with BLK (wrong colour) rigged to have **more** images (4) than TAN (correct, 3).
